screens.headline: Set up your display for SDR
instructions: Turn off HDR and auto colour management in Windows display settings.
Dim the room and sit where you normally watch. Use the display's recommended resolution.
Turn off Game, Vivid and Dynamic modes, motion smoothing and contrast enhancers.
EyeCal checks SDR by eye. A meter is needed to measure colour accuracy.
screens.should_see: You should see four evenly progressing grey patches.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: two grey patches merge.
screens.question: Ready to check your display?

screens.headline: Check the RGB range
instructions: Compare the dark top row and bright bottom row. Match the source and display RGB range.
screens.should_see: You should see steps in both rows, although the first dark steps can be subtle.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: dark and bright steps are crushed.
screens.question: How do the two rows look?
display_hints: Look for RGB range in your GPU control panel.
Look for HDMI Black Level or RGB Range on the TV, then match the GPU control panel.
Look for an RGB range or HDMI black-level option on the projector. Match the GPU setting.

screens.headline: Adjust brightness for shadow detail
instructions: Use the display's black-level or brightness control. Raise it until the darkest steps start to separate, then back off if black turns grey.
Full-range PC output starts at code 0. This pattern compares above-black steps against 0.
screens.should_see: You should see some above-black strips while the background stays black.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: the darkest strips disappear.
screens.question: How does the black level look?
display_hints: Use a neutral room and disable automatic contrast.
Try the display's black-level control. Keep local dimming and shadow enhancement consistent.
Dim the room first. Stray light can hide small differences near black.

screens.headline: Lower contrast until the whites separate
instructions: Lower the display contrast if the brightest steps merge into one white area.
screens.should_see: You should see small steps all the way to the brightest white.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: several top steps have merged.
screens.question: Can you separate the bright steps?

screens.headline: Match the fine pattern to the solid grey
instructions: Sit at your usual distance. If the checkerboard is visible, step back or squint slightly.
screens.should_see: You should see similar brightness in each top checker and the matching solid below.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: the solid patches are too light.
screens.question: How do the solid patches look?

settings.label: Target
descriptions: sRGB: the standard target for typical computer content.
2.2: a simple target for general viewing.
BT.1886: for dark-room TVs. This approximation assumes ideal black.

screens.headline: Check clean edges and the whole border
instructions: Reduce sharpening until the halos disappear. Disable overscan or select the display's 1:1 mode if the border is cropped.
screens.should_see: You should see crisp individual lines, one clean edge, four corners, and a mark on each screen edge.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: bright and dark halos hug the edge.
screens.question: How does the pattern look?

screens.headline: Look for bands in the baseline ramp
instructions: Keep dither off for this first pass. Look for broad bands, not individual pixels.
screens.should_see: You should see a continuous-looking transition from black to white.
screens.bad_example: Bad example: large stripes interrupt the transition.
screens.question: How does the baseline look?

screens.headline: Compare dither on and off
instructions: Drag the divider handle. Click the dither button or press D to change methods.
screens.should_see: Left uses no dither. Fine texture on the right can make bands less visible.
screens.bad_example: Compare both sides at the same brightness along each vertical ramp.
screens.question: Which side looks smoother?

screens.headline: Compare 8-bit and 10-bit output
instructions: Use B or the button. F1 shows the format and fullscreen mode.
Turn off HDR and auto colour management before comparing.
screens.should_see: The ramp should show the same range in both passes.
screens.bad_example: Broad bands with no improvement are a clue only in granted Vulkan exclusive mode.
screens.question: Which pass looked smoother?

screens.headline: Check the shadows and midtones
instructions: The top ramp covers near-black. The lower ramp compares mid-grey. Press M or use the button to check the moving version.
screens.should_see: Look for steps, moving grain, or flicker and note which region shows it.
screens.bad_example: Look for coarse bands or moving texture that distracts from the gradient.
screens.question: Where do you see bands?
